title: Graphic Storytelling — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of Graphic Storytelling's rich face: a strip whose layout your hands time, blind, against McCloud's time-is-space, and the two Daily Page roughs that put the color claims to a viewer, laid beside the sections they test, with the fingerprint of the words each was made against so the page can say when a piece may lag the text. I grow when the entry is enriched again, and I expect to be re-tuned when the page's revision lands; I never hold the entry's words.

offers.what: "Time is rendered as space — a wider panel, or more gutter before the next, simply lasts longer" is stronger than McCloud, and its gutter half is not located in his book. In Understanding Comics ch. 4 (about pp. 99–101) he says a panel's durations are "defined more by the contents of the panel than by the panel itself", that shape differences don't change a panel's meaning in time but "can affect the reading experience", and that a lengthened panel has "the feeling of greater length". These are quoted from memory of the book, confirmed only in part by a secondary summary, so check them against the pages first. No passage was found for the gutter clause; course pages teach it, but not as his. A possible sentence: "time is drawn as space: a wider panel can feel longer, though McCloud says a panel's contents set its time more than its shape", with the gutter clause attributed to the craft or held until it is found. The revision draft repeats the same sentence ("A wider panel, or more gutter, simply lasts longer"), so this applies when it lands too. The time-is-space piece times the two halves apart; no reader has run it yet, so there are no numbers.

offers.section: The live edge — black-and-white, plus one bold color
offers.what: "Restraint as the source of the punch" is contradicted in part by the gathered color hold (2026-10-28, one viewer, scored out of 5): red held from the first panel 3, below all ink 4; red withheld and revealed on the close-up's downbeat 5; full palette 2. Restraint beat the full palette, as the page says, but alone it lost to no color at all. What hit hardest was the withheld color, revealed on the beat. The baton and the revision draft already carry this; it is recorded here so it isn't lost if the revision waits.
The comment "CLAUDE → LOUDON: hero + icon pending" under the title is stale: the hero and icon exist in the bundle. The revision draft drops it.

verdicts.why: A real test with a working size control, and it walks up, but its verdict lines overclaim one run: with a true equal 1.3× effect at 25% scatter it says "your holds split them" in 33% of runs and "time was not drawn as space" in 51%. Split only when h(wide)/h(gutter) clears ×1.1 in all three stories (≤1/8 by chance), soften the failure line, state that either half showing longer has a ≤1/4 chance, and add the equal-effect check to check.mjs.

pieces.by: the Maker · SVG ink strips, timed by hand
pieces.title: Does a wider panel last longer?
pieces.caption: **McCloud's line, put to your hands.** It walks up from two panels and the gap you fill (closure), through a strip whose layout you drag while its drawing stays still, to a stopwatch you hold. Then fifteen strips: three small stories, each in five layouts, shuffled, each at a slightly different size. For each one you hold for as long as the wait felt, and the layouts are compared only after the last hold. The wide panel and the wide gutter each add the same length along the reading line. A tall panel adds the same paper across it, the control that tells space along the line from plain size. It can come out against the page, and it can split the sentence's two halves, panel and gutter. One reader, fifteen holds: a reading, not a law.

pieces.title: The color hold · Daily Page rough, 2026-10-28
pieces.caption: **The color hold, as it was played.** Five blind takes of one six-panel ink strip on an 84 bpm clock, differing only in where one red sits and on which beat it arrives; the key shows after you rate. Loudon's scores, one viewer, one sitting, out of 5: red withheld and revealed on the close-up's downbeat 5; all ink 4; red two beats late 4; red held from the first panel 3; full palette 2. The full palette lost, as the next paragraph says, but restraint alone didn't win: the same red held from the start scored below no color at all. What hit hardest was the color withheld, then revealed on the beat. It plays a kick on the clock after a click; no agent has heard it.

pieces.title: One strip, six stories · Daily Page rough, 2026-10-29
pieces.caption: **A color script you can play.** The same six frames, drawing and clock, with color the only variable. Four takes hold one palette throughout (anger, nostalgia, wistfulness, depression). Two move it across the panels, warming toward the end or draining toward it: a color script in six frames. In Loudon's sit the two arcs carried far more than the moods, and the draining one was the clearest story and "by far" the most emotional. The warming one failed because the drawing contradicted it: a tool can't carry a meaning the other tools contradict. One viewer, one sitting. Its answers live in the frame and are lost on a reload, so copy them out before you leave. It plays sound after a click; no agent has heard it.
